title: Sugarcane Farmers Block Highways Across Karnataka for Higher Prices

tea.why: Protesting low prices for sugarcane and lack of a concrete decision after discussions with union ministers.
tea.want: Higher prices, increased MSP, Fair and Remunerative Price, Swaminathan Commission recommendations, and a State Advisory Price.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar met the padayatra in Kittur and promised a stakeholder meeting after Dasara, but leaders stated the march would continue.

summary: Sugarcane farmers staged protests and blocked national highways across several districts in Karnataka, including Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, and Dharwad. The agitators disrupted traffic on key routes, such as the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway, demanding increased Minimum Support Prices, fair and remunerative pricing, and implementation of the Swaminathan Commission recommendations. The protests followed a failed meeting between farmer representatives and union ministers in Delhi. Organised partly by groups like Hasiru Sene and Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, participants vowed to continue their agitation until their demands are met. In response, Union Food Minister Pralhad Joshi appealed for an end to the demonstrations, while Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar later met the protesting farmers in Kittur, promising to convene a meeting of all stakeholders following the Dasara festival.
demands: Determination of the Fair and Remunerative Price
Implementation of the Swaminathan Commission recommendations
State Advisory Price of ₹1,000 per tonne supplied
response: Union Food Minister Pralhad Joshi appealed to farmers to withdraw the agitation, assuring government support. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar met protesters in Kittur, appealing to them to end their march and promising a stakeholder meeting after Dasara.

updates.text: Sugarcane farmers blocked national highways across multiple districts in Karnataka, demanding higher produce prices.
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar met farmers undertaking a padayatra in Kittur and promised a stakeholder meeting after Dasara.
